docs.title: mobileAX
docs.text:
A millisecond-latency CLI for driving Android devices. Built for LLM agents and shell scripts.

mobileAX is the smallest thing that gives you a tap, a type, and a wait on a real Android device, from any language. It is one Rust CLI on the host and one small jar on the device — no installed app, no root, no WebDriver server. A single call costs a few milliseconds.

This guide reads as a story. Start at the top.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The standard ways to drive an Android device are heavy. adb shell input tap X Y works for coordinates but can't find a button by label. uiautomator2 makes you install two APKs and speaks only Python. Appium asks you to bring up a WebDriver server and then pays ~100 ms per click on top of that. None of these were designed for the case that's most common today: an LLM loop or a shell script that wants to call tap("Continue") thousands of times in an afternoon.

mobileAX is designed exactly for that loop. You drop one jar on the device, the daemon stays warm under app_process, and the CLI talks to it over a length-prefixed binary protocol. A round trip is 2–7 ms. Every action verb returns a structured exit code so unattended scripts can branch without parsing stderr.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
You need adb on $PATH (brew install android-platform-tools on macOS, the matching android-tools package on Linux). Then:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pbk20191/mobileax/main/install.sh | bash

USB debugging on, plug the phone in, confirm adb devices lists it, and you're ready.

docs.title: The agent loop
docs.text:
This is the one passage to read if you read nothing else.

mobax use                 # auto-detect a device, start the daemon
mobax ui                  # flat table of tappable nodes — drop into an LLM
mobax tap "Continue"      # the LLM picks a label, you tap it
mobax wait "Welcome"      # block on the next screen
mobax drop                # tear it all down

mobax ui (since v0.1.14 the interactive table is the default) returns one line per actionable node:

fill  EditText  "Email"     #email     540,540
fill  EditText  "Password"  #password  540,640  [password]
tap   Button    "Continue"  #continue  540,860

Hand that to a model, get back a label, hand the label to mobax tap. That's the loop. The full XML hierarchy is still one flag away (mobax ui --xml), but for an LLM the flat table is roughly 10× cheaper in tokens.

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
When labels collide or you need a more specific match, mobax find and the selector-aware verbs accept a CSS-like grammar. The vocabulary is borrowed from Playwright's locator API on purpose, so muscle memory transfers.

mobax tap 'Button[text="Sign in"]'                   # exact text
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Sign in")'               # substring (Playwright sugar)
mobax tap 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email])'     # relational
mobax tap 'Button:near(ImageView[desc~=cart], 200)'  # within 200 px
mobax tap '[role=Switch][state=Off]'                 # Compose role / state

Compose and androidx widgets expose a role and a state (in the device's language: 스위치 / 사용 안함 on a Korean device), and mobax ui shows them next to each row. The full set of pseudo-classes (:visible, :clickable, :editable, :heading, :in(), :below(), :right-of(), :near(), :has-text(), :text-is()) is documented in the cookbook.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
Every action verb honours the same set of flags so RPA scripts stop hand-rolling retry loops:

mobax tap "Refresh" --visible --unique --timeout 3s --retries 4 --retry-delay 500ms

Failures funnel through structured exit codes:

Code Meaning 0 ok 1 failure (everything below not broken out — full code in error.code when --json) 2 NOT_FOUND 3 TIMEOUT 4 AMBIGUOUS — --unique saw more than one match

That deliberate small alphabet is the thing scripts actually branch on. The full structured ErrCode lives in JSON-mode output for any caller that wants to dispatch on the long tail (DAEMON_ERROR, SECURE_WINDOW, BAD_ARG, etc.).

docs.title: JSON output and language bindings
docs.text:
--json (or HS_FORMAT=json) makes every action verb emit one structured line:

{"verb":"tap","ok":true,"result":{"x":540,"y":860,"text":"Continue"}}
{"verb":"tap","ok":false,"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","detail":"no node matched"}}

That's the shape any subprocess driver should consume. A first-party Python SDK lives under bindings/python/; other languages can drive the CLI in ~30 lines of subprocess code.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
host                                  device (shell UID, app_process)
─────                                  ──────────────────────────────
mobax <verb> ──► adb server ─────►     MobaxServer → Dispatch (one coroutine per connection)
                                       ├─ Server.respond     sync verbs (Pm Am Wm Props Providers …)
                                       ├─ Gestures           input, wait_for_*, tap_and_*
                                       ├─ Transfers          push/pull, install, uninstall
                                       ├─ ProcStream         dumpsys logcat shell monitor clip_watch
                                       ├─ Streams            stream, stream_tilejpeg, stream_h264
                                       ├─ State + StateRefresher  (push-cached snapshot, state_watch)
                                       └─ UiEvents / Waits   (accessibility event fan-out)

The daemon runs as the shell UID via app_process with hidden-API restrictions lifted.

There is a second build of the same daemon, and mobax use prefers it where mobaxd.apk sits next to the jar and the device runs Android 10+: an installed APK (dev.mobileax.daemon) run as an instrumentation. If it can't be installed (no "Install via USB") or doesn't start, use falls back to the jar; use --instr|--jar (or MOBAX_DAEMON=instr|jar) picks one. use installs it when the device's copy isn't this build and starts am instrument -w --no-hidden-api-checks … /.MobaxInstrumentation. UiAutomation comes from the framework (shared with UiAutomator's UiDevice), shell permissions are adopted (adoptShellPermissionIdentity), and what needs the shell uid itself (dumpsys, settings, logcat, cp) runs through a framework-started sh. It exits when its am instrument process goes. Three Gradle modules: daemon/core is the daemon (a library), daemon/shell the app_process entry point and context setup (build/mobax.jar), daemon/instr the instrumentation's (build/mobaxd.apk). Each entry point sets Host.current (its Context, calling package, startup log and shell) and calls serve(). The shell is where they differ most: the jar spawns sh -c as its own child, the APK goes through UiAutomation.

On a physical device either build leaves once no client has been connected for 30 s (Lease), so unplugging the cable or quitting the host frees the device's UiAutomation for other tools. Connections that stay open hold it: the state watcher use spawns, the MCP server's pooled sessions, a mirror. The next use, or any verb that finds no daemon, starts it again. An emulator keeps its daemon until drop. use --idle-exit S (or MOBAX_IDLE_EXIT=S) overrides either default; 0 keeps it up.

Either build listens on the abstract Unix socket @mobaxd_<port> (the host opens it through the adb server: host:transport:SERIAL, then localabstract:mobaxd_<port>, with no host port forward) and refuses any peer whose SO_PEERCRED uid isn't shell or root. The host runs a background state-daemon that subscribes to state_watch and atomically rewrites ~/.mobileax/state-<port>.json on every event-driven refresh. mobax info / mobax info / mobax show all read straight out of that file.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
One main thread runs Looper.loop(). Sockets, process pipes and the dumpsys pipe are registered with the main MessageQueue (epoll) through Io; each connection is a Conn driven by a coroutine on Dispatchers.Main. Accessibility events, display/package/config listeners, ImageReader and MediaCodec callbacks, and all timers (delay) run there too. Nothing on the main thread may block.

Everything off main runs on the kotlinx-coroutines scheduler, so all of it shares one worker pool (DefaultDispatcher-worker-N):

  • Loop.Work (Default.limitedParallelism(≤4)): CPU work and binder calls that can take long — JPEG/PNG encoding, tile diffs, accessibility tree dumps, PackageInstaller and file I/O.
  • Loop.Blocking (IO): calls that wait on a peer — binder dumps into a pipe a slow client drains, MediaCodec / VirtualDisplay setup and teardown.
  • Loop.FrameCopy (IO.limitedParallelism(1)): mirror pixel copies, which block on the GPU fence once per frame.

Gestures pace MOVE events on Choreographer vsync callbacks; stream fps=N sends on the first vsync after each slot. state_watch and clip_watch collect StateFlows (one clipboard poller per interval, only while watched).

Output is queued per connection: send applies backpressure past 4 MiB; sendLatest keeps only the newest unsent frame (JPEG stream, state_watch). stream_h264 connections with the same parameters share one encoder; each access unit is copied once. Joiners and lagging viewers restart from cached SPS/PPS + the frames since the last IDR, so the shared encoder never waits.

wire-smoke.py run / diff (in scripts/) records normalized responses for every verb so two daemon builds can be compared on a device.

docs.text:

daemon/shell/, daemon/instr/  its app_process and am-instrument entry points
mobax-cli/                 host CLI — short-verb surface (`mobax use`, `mobax see`, …)
mobax-viewer/              GUI mirror — winit + GPU decode (Metal/VideoToolbox, D3D11/MF, GLES/VA-API)
build.gradle.kts              AGP: kotlinc → R8 → build/mobax.jar, build/mobaxd.apk  (build.sh wraps it)

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-05-24 with n=50 on the Android 15 emulator Google sdk_gphone64_arm64 (1440x3120, SDK 35), host macOS/aarch64. Numbers are p50 with p95 in parentheses. mobax uses one warm daemon socket; adb starts a fresh adb CLI process per sample.

Reproduce the mobileAX side with mobax bench -n 50 or machine-readable mobax bench -n 50 --json. Reproduce raw ADB baselines with scripts/bench-adb.sh -n 50; the script keeps the exact ADB commands inspectable.

The default mobax bench suite follows the hot path: 768px JPEG screenshots for agents, with WebP as a lossy export comparison. PNG is intentionally left out of the headline mobax suite because Android's PNG encoder is a debug/export path, not an interaction loop path.

docs.title: Agent Token/Turn Benchmark
docs.text:
What an agent pays per task over MCP (mobax mcp): calls and approximate response tokens. scripts/agent-bench.py replays the fixed tool-call sequences in bench/agent/*.json (the fewest calls today's tools need, then a check). No LLM runs, so it is free and repeatable. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-agent-first-direction.md.

  • Approximate tokens = ASCII chars / 4 (rounded up) + one per non-ASCII char. A fixed yardstick for comparing runs, not a tokenizer; changing it means re-recording the baseline.
  • A step may name expect: text its reply must contain (a toast, a result only the reply shows); without it the step fails.
  • setup steps are not counted. They may call host adb ({"adb": [...]}), since MCP has no device shell.
  • Tokens and time are medians over runs. Action replies report what changed on screen, which depends on timing, so tokens vary a little from run to run.
  • Stable means: calls identical, total tokens within ±5%. The ±% column is the run-to-run spread; above 5% it is marked ! and printed as UNSTABLE, but does not fail the run. s2 (whether the 4th swipe still scrolls), s3 and s4 (camera start-up after the permission tap) routinely exceed it: the action replies differ, not the calls.
  • Fixed before this baseline (fix/open-settle): open could report "settled" on an empty screen (a cold start past its 6 s settle) or on the screen before it (a late event from home); the next tap missed. A slow emulator (a long-running one with its guest swapping, or a busy host) makes every action several times slower: cold-boot it before measuring.
  • Twice, during s4 (the camera), the system watchdog killed system_server (Blocked in monitor WindowManagerService), and the emulator's camera HAL aborted right after. Not yet told apart from a cause in mobax. Since 4c28b14 the daemon exits with system_server and the next call starts a fresh one (seen working here); a cold boot clears the leftover state.
  • s1 lands on 651 or 817 tokens per session (no spread within one): the tap's reply differs between sessions. Compare s1 across sessions with care.
./gradlew benchToastApk        # s6's app → build/bench-toast.apk; run from the repo root
ANDROID_HOME=… python -I scripts/agent-bench.py --runs 3 --compare bench/agent/baseline.json

Baseline (2026-11-04, emulator Medium_Phone, SDK 36, ko-KR, host GPU, fresh cold boot, idle host; mobax from fix/open-settle, 3 runs; bench/agent/baseline.json). A repeat run and a reversed-order run stayed within ±5% on the total (+3.6%, +2.7%) with identical calls:

Scenario Calls Tokens (p50) ± (max−min) Time (p50) s1-settings-item 3 651 0 2.3 s s2-long-list 8 1847 5 7.6 s s3-search-form 5 1297 1 4.4 s s4-permission-popup 5 526 116 2.9 s s5-heavy-screen 3 260 0 0.8 s total 24 4581 tools/list (once per session) 2668 Scenario Task Measures s1 Settings → "디스플레이 및 터치" basic navigation s2 Accessibility list, last item (tap with scroll: true; the baseline used 4 swipes) scrolling (later: find-with-scroll) s3 Settings search "배터리" → result typing, result check s4 Fresh camera: location-tag prompt, location permission (no wait: a missed tap looks again while the screen moves) popups (later: auto-handling) s5 Recents (two fixed cards), one ui output size of a full-screen system UI s6 The bench app (bench/toast-app) → tap its one button; the check is the reply carrying toast: a result shown only as a toast

s6 used Settings' Build number until the instrumentation daemon became the default: it runs the device as a monkey, and Settings ignores Build number taps then. Its tokens (about 100 now, 338–648 before) don't compare with older runs.

Findings from writing the scenarios:

  • A bare-word target (다음, Gmail) is read as a class-name selector and misses; scenarios use :has-text("…").
  • The tool list (2668, every session) is more than half of all five scenarios' replies together (4554): the cheapest cut is in tool descriptions.
  • Settings search is its own package (com.google.android.settings.intelligence).
  • wait returning at once while a page is still settling makes the first swipe land at a slightly different scroll position each run.

docs.title: Cookbook
docs.text:
Recipes for driving Android with mobax. Each one is copy-pasteable into a real terminal.

These build on the agent loop in the README and the verb table in mobax --help. If you've never run mobax use, start there. The shared action flags (--timeout, --retries, --visible, --unique, --nth, --json, …) work on every action verb; this page shows them in context rather than restating the table.

docs.title: Fast agent loop
docs.text:
Use the UI table as the primary model input. It is small, text-first, and already contains the center coordinates mobileAX will tap.

mobax use
mobax ui > /tmp/mobax-screen.txt

Only add an image when the visual layout matters. Keep it agent-sized:

mobax see --size 768 /tmp/mobax-screen.jpg

mobax see out.jpg without --size is a native-resolution export for bug reports and pixel debugging. It is slower and much larger than the 768px agent path. PNG is lossless/debug only:

mobax see --native /tmp/full.jpg
mobax see --native /tmp/full.png

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text:
The canonical flow: find the email field, fill it, find the password field, fill it, submit, and wait for the dashboard.

mobax use
mobax wait idle 200ms

mobax tap   "Sign in"              --visible --unique --timeout 5s
mobax fill  '#email'                'you@example.com'   # same as [id=email]
mobax fill  'EditText[resource-id=com.example:id/password]' "hunter2"
mobax submit
mobax wait  "Dashboard"            --timeout 15s

If the app has two "Sign in" buttons (header and footer, for example), --unique will fail with exit 4 (AMBIGUOUS); pick the one you want with --nth 1 or tighten the selector. When IDs aren't stable, lean on the relational pseudo-classes:

mobax fill 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email])'    "you@example.com"
mobax fill 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Password])' "hunter2"

fill waits for its field like tap does. Some fields refuse set-text while they are still opening (a search view, for one); fill then clicks the field, lets it settle and sets it again, and as a last resort types the text (ASCII) or pastes it (anything else).

If the field already has focus and you want the real keyboard path rather than atomic set-text, use type:

mobax type "you@example.com"
mobax submit

docs.title: Waiting for the next screen
docs.text:
mobax wait is overloaded by argument shape so it stays readable:

mobax wait idle 200ms        # block until the UI settles for 200 ms
mobax wait "Welcome"         # block until that text appears anywhere
mobax wait com.foo           # block until that package is in the foreground
mobax wait com.foo/.MainAct  # block on a specific activity
mobax wait 500ms             # client-side sleep (no daemon hop)
mobax wait '#results'        # block until a node matches a selector
mobax wait 'Button[text="OK"]'

Text waits match case-sensitively ("Battery Saver" isn't "Battery saver"); copy the label from mobax ui.

All forms honour --timeout. The default is 10 s — bump it for slow launches. Prefer these waits over shell sleep; a fixed sleep is both slower on fast devices and flaky on slow ones.

docs.title: Do then verify in one call
docs.text:
Tap a button and only succeed if the expected next state appears. This is the usual replacement for tap && sleep && wait chains:

mobax act --tap   "Send"          --until "Sent"             --timeout 8s
mobax act --fill  '[id=q]' "llm"  --until-selector RecyclerView --timeout 5s
mobax act --swipe up 300          --until-idle               --timeout 2s

Exit 0 only if both halves succeeded. TIMEOUT means the predicate never appeared; NOT_FOUND means the action itself could not execute.

docs.title: Retrying a flaky tap
docs.text:
Daemon-side waits get retried automatically when a TIMEOUT comes back, so the script stays linear:

mobax tap  "Refresh" --retries 4 --retry-delay 500ms --timeout 3s
mobax wait "Synced"  --retries 4 --timeout 5s

For unattended jobs, branch on the exit code instead of parsing stderr. There are only three codes worth a case arm:

mobax tap "Submit" --unique --timeout 5s
case $? in
  0)  echo "submitted" ;;
  2)  echo "no Submit button on screen" ;;        # NOT_FOUND
  3)  echo "tap acked but UI hung — escalating"   # TIMEOUT
      mobax see --size 768 /tmp/hung.jpg ;;
  4)  echo "ambiguous — narrow the selector" ;;   # AMBIGUOUS
  *)  echo "unexpected failure"; exit 1 ;;
esac

The full structured ErrCode (DAEMON_ERROR, PRECONDITION, SECURE_WINDOW, …) is preserved in --json output as error.code — use that when you need to dispatch on the long tail.

docs.title: Scrolling until something is visible
docs.text:
When the match is in the tree but below (or above) the screen, mobax tap swipes toward it and looks again, up to six times. Long lists only keep the rows near the screen in the tree, though (a RecyclerView recycles the rest), so for a row far down, scroll first. A 12-attempt scroll-then-tap loop in five lines:

for _ in $(seq 1 12); do
  mobax tap "Settings" --visible --unique --timeout 500ms && break
  mobax swipe up 250
done

If you already know one scroll is enough, batch the scroll and tap over a single warm socket:

mobax run - <<'EOF'
set timeout=500ms
swipe up 250
tap "Settings" --visible --unique
EOF

mobax run executes one command per line. Do not put multiple verbs on one line with semicolons. Use the shell for loop above when you need conditional looping.

docs.title: Debugging selectors
docs.text:
Start broad, inspect the JSON, then tighten. This is faster than guessing at coordinates.

mobax find 'Button:has-text("Continue")' --json | jq .
mobax find '*[text=Continue], *[text=Next]' --visible --json | jq .

If there are multiple matches, either make the selector structural or pick an index explicitly:

mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Continue"):in(LinearLayout[id~=footer])' --unique
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Continue")' --visible --nth 2

Other ways to narrow it down:

mobax tap 'LinearLayout:has(TextView[text=Wi-Fi])'      # the row holding the label (innermost row only)
mobax tap '[text="continue" i]'                           # case-insensitive
mobax tap '[text=/^(log|sign) ?in$/i]'                    # regex (search; anchor with ^ $)
mobax fill 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email])' me@x    # nearest field under the label comes first

docs.title: Two-factor SMS
docs.text:
mobax sms reads the inbox directly via IContentProvider — no installed helper app, no permission grants.

mobax wait "Enter the code"
CODE=$(mobax sms inbox --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].body' | grep -oE '[0-9]{6}')
mobax type   "$CODE"
mobax submit

For apps that put the code on the clipboard, read or paste it directly:

CODE=$(mobax clip)
mobax type "$CODE"
mobax paste 'EditText:focused'

Clipboard watch is useful for magic-link and OTP handoff scripts:

mobax clip --watch --interval 250

docs.title: Notifications and push flows
docs.text:
Trigger a server-side push, then read recent notifications. Filter by package when you know it:

mobax notif com.example.app --limit 5 --json | jq .
mobax notif --history --limit 20 --json | jq .

For login links that open a browser or app, wait on the resulting package or activity instead of sleeping:

mobax wait com.example.app --timeout 15s
mobax wait com.example.app/.MainActivity --timeout 15s

docs.title: Running against many devices
docs.text:
mobax fan runs the same verb against each serial in parallel and exits non-zero if any device fails:

mobax fan PIXEL6,PIXEL7,EMU -- tap "Continue" --visible --timeout 5s

For machine-readable per-device output, add the global --json:

mobax --json fan PIXEL6,EMU -- wait "Welcome" --timeout 10s | jq -c

docs.title: Screenshotting on failure
docs.text:
A one-line bash -e trap that captures whatever was on screen the moment a verb failed. Use the fast 768px JPEG path for unattended runs:

set -e
trap 'mobax see --size 768 /tmp/mobileax-$$-failure.jpg' ERR

mobax tap  "Sign in" --unique
mobax wait "Dashboard" --timeout 10s

When you need a full artifact bundle for CI, collect the UI, device state, logs, and screenshot together:

DIR=/tmp/mobileax-failure-$$
mkdir -p "$DIR"
trap 'mobax ui --json > "$DIR/ui.json"; mobax ui --xml > "$DIR/ui.xml"; mobax info > "$DIR/info.txt"; mobax logs --tail 200 > "$DIR/logs.txt"; mobax see --size 768 "$DIR/screen.jpg"; echo "$DIR"' ERR

If you expect a black screenshot from a banking, password, or incognito screen, opt into the slower FLAG_SECURE check:

mobax see --secure-check --size 768 /tmp/secure-check.jpg

docs.title: Selectors when text alone isn't enough
docs.text:
Real Android UIs rarely give you stable resource IDs. Lean on the relational pseudo-classes:

# The OK button inside a specific dialog:
mobax tap '*[text="OK"]:in(LinearLayout[id~=dialog])' --unique

# The EditText below the "Email" label, visible only:
mobax tap 'EditText:below(TextView[text=Email]):visible' --unique

# Buttons near a specific icon:
mobax find 'Button:near(ImageView[desc~=cart], 200)'

# OR groups — "Continue" or "Next", whichever shipped this build:
mobax tap '*[text=Continue], *[text=Next]' --visible --unique --timeout 5s

# Playwright-style sugar:
mobax tap 'Button:has-text("Sign in")'
mobax tap 'Button:text-is("Sign in")'

docs.title: Driving from Python
docs.text:
There's a first-party SDK that wraps the CLI as a context manager and maps the exit codes to typed exceptions:

# pip install ./bindings/python  (from a checkout)
from mobileax import Session, NotFound, Timeout

with Session() as d:
    d.tap("Continue", visible=True, unique=True, timeout="5s")
    d.fill("[resource-id=com.example:id/email]", "you@example.com")
    d.submit()
    try:
        d.wait(text="Dashboard", timeout="15s")
    except Timeout:
        d.go("back")

For tight loops, the SDK opens a warm-socket batching context that shares one mobax run - subprocess across calls — per-call process startup collapses into one startup for the whole batch:

with Session() as d:
    with d.batch(timeout="5s", retries=2) as b:
        for label in labels:
            b.tap(label, visible=True)
        b.wait(text="Done")

For Node, Go, or anything else, drive mobax --json as a subprocess and parse one JSON line per call:

import json, subprocess
r = subprocess.run(
    ["mobax", "--json", "tap", "Sign in", "--visible", "--unique", "--timeout", "5s"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
match r.returncode:
    case 0: print("tapped at", json.loads(r.stdout)["result"]["x"])
    case 2: raise RuntimeError("no Sign-in button on screen")
    case 3: raise TimeoutError("tap timed out")

docs.title: Batch scripts
docs.text:
For longer flows where the per-call socket churn matters, mobax run reads verb lines from a file (or stdin) and executes them over one warm socket. The set directives raise defaults without touching every line:

# flow.mobax
set timeout=8s
set retries=2
set continue-on-error
set dump-ttl=200ms

wait idle
tap   "Continue"   --visible --unique
fill  [id=email]   "you@example.com"
fill  [id=pw]      "hunter2"
submit
wait  "Dashboard"  --timeout 15s

mobax init my-flow.mobax       # scaffold a starter file
mobax run  my-flow.mobax       # run it

For ad-hoc batching, pipe directly:

printf '%s\n' 'tap "Refresh"' 'wait "Synced"' | mobax run -

docs.title: App lifecycle setup
docs.text:
Bring an app to the foreground, close it, or use raw shell commands for setup that is not yet a first-class verb. Pipe shell commands into mobax shell so streamed command output is drained correctly:

mobax open com.example.app/.MainActivity
mobax close com.example.app
printf '%s\n' 'pm clear com.example.app' | mobax shell

For deeplink-driven flows, inspect what the APK declares:

mobax links com.example.app
mobax open com.example.app/.MainActivity

docs.title: Emulators and the Android CLI
docs.text: mobileAX drives any device adb can see, API 28 or later. For emulators the recommended setup is Google's Android CLI (android) plus an AVD that renders on the host GPU.

docs.title: Android CLI
docs.text:
Install the android CLI (on Windows: winget install Google.AndroidCLI). mobax uses it to find adb, so nothing has to be on PATH:

android info                  # sdk: <path>  — adb is <path>/platform-tools/adb
android emulator list         # AVDs
android emulator start NAME   # returns once the emulator has booted
android emulator stop NAME

android emulator start takes --cold (skip the snapshot) and --headless (no window); android emulator create makes new AVDs (--help lists its options).

docs.title: Host GPU, always
docs.text:
Run emulators with host GPU rendering. android emulator start has no -gpu option, so set it in the AVD's config, ~/.android/avd/NAME.avd/config.ini:

hw.gpu.mode=host

Starting the emulator directly, pass it on the command line instead:

emulator -avd NAME -gpu host

To make it the default for every AVD, whoever starts it, turn the matching feature flags on in ~/.android/advancedFeatures.ini (create it if missing):

ForceGpuHost = on
Vulkan = on
GLDirectMem = on

ForceGpuHost puts the emulator on the host GPU even when the AVD says auto (the emulator's verbose log then shows gpu_mode_requested: host). Watch the spelling: the emulator silently ignores names it doesn't know, EnforceHostGPU included. Vulkan exposes host Vulkan to the guest; GLDirectMem maps guest GL buffers straight to host memory instead of copying them.

The default auto can choose a slower renderer. Every mirror frame is read back from the GPU (the daemon's main cost for stream), so the renderer shows up directly in frame rates, and numbers from different GPU modes aren't comparable.

docs.title: CPU and memory
docs.text:
The stock phone AVD has 4 cores and 2 GB. More helps: JPEG encoding, the app under test and SurfaceFlinger all share the guest's CPUs. In the same config.ini:

hw.cpu.ncore=6      # the emulator caps cores at 6
hw.ramSize=4096

On a Windows host (API 36 x86_64 AVD, 1080×2400, -gpu host) going from 4 cores / 2 GB to 6 cores / 4 GB took a native-size jpeg stream from 25–28 to 29–32 fps, --size 1200 from 42–50 to 56 fps, and h264 from 24 to 50 fps.

docs.title: Stream size
docs.text: At native resolution the mirror's GPU readback (25–36 ms per 1080×2400 frame on that host) caps a JPEG stream near 30 fps. Asking for a smaller frame cuts the readback, the encode and the decode together: mobax-viewer --size 1200 reaches about 56 fps, and the window rarely shows more pixels than that. h264 avoids the readback entirely.

docs.title: How mobax finds adb
docs.text:
In order, resolved once per process:

  1. $MOBILEAX_ADB, then $ADB
  2. ~/.mobileax/adb-path — the cached result of 3 (android info takes ~0.7 s)
  3. android info → <sdk>/platform-tools/adb
  4. $ANDROID_HOME, then $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT
  5. adb on PATH
  6. Android Studio's default SDK (~/Library/Android/sdk, ~/Android/Sdk, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk)

The last step is for MCP hosts and other GUI apps, which often start mobax without the shell's PATH. See also Sharp edges.

docs.title: Sharp edges
docs.text:
• Settings provider rejects our app_process identity; SettingsDirect uses IActivityManager.getContentProviderExternal (the cmd content path).
  • am start goes via IActivityTaskManager.startActivityAsUser with callingPackage="com.android.shell"; the system Context can't host startActivity from our anonymous process.
  • The instrumentation build (mobax use's default where mobaxd.apk is found; --instr to insist, --jar to skip it):
  • It is an installed APK (dev.mobileax.daemon, Android 10 / SDK 29 or later). Some OEMs need "Install via USB" (or similar) enabled once before it can be installed; until then use runs the jar. mobax drop uninstalls it (--keep-apk keeps it).
  • One per device: UiAutomation has one connection. A second mobax use --instr --port N is refused; a UiAutomator test (or uiautomator dump) started while it runs is cut off.
  • Monkey mode is on while it runs (ActivityManager.isUserAMonkey()); AMS clears it when the daemon goes.
  • It is an app uid with adopted shell permissions: binder calls name its own package as callingPackage, it declares QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, and what needs the shell uid goes through Shell. On SDK 34+ that is executeShellCommandRwe, which does no quoting, so the script goes in on stdin as one line; on SDK 29–33 the script, stdin data, stderr, exit code and pid are files in the app's external files/shell/ directory and executeShellCommand runs sh <file>. -e shell file on am instrument forces the file path.
  • Off-screen nodes: a list keeps a few rows past the screen in the tree. They are in dump with off (and mobax find prints [off-screen below]); wait and the daemon's node actions (node_click, wait_for_text, …) treat them as not there yet; tap scrolls toward one and taps it. Rows the list hasn't made yet are in no tree: scroll (scroll: true, swipe).
  • The screenshot mirror is made on demand, not kept up: a mirror recomposites every frame the screen changes (SDK 36 while scrolling: surfaceflinger about twice the CPU, the emulator ~15% more). Streams make one and hold it; screenshots use one that is up, or make one when three come within 5 s; one unused for 30 s is closed. Single screenshots go through DisplayCapture below (~20-40 ms more than a warm mirror).
  • Screenshots without a mirror (no CAPTURE_VIDEO_OUTPUT and no SurfaceControl display): see and element screenshots ask SurfaceFlinger for one frame at the size sent (DisplayCapture: IWindowManager.captureDisplay on 34+, SurfaceControl.captureDisplay on 31–33, SurfaceControl.screenshot on 29–30), which needs only READ_FRAME_BUFFER; then UiAutomation.takeScreenshot. The 29–30 call can't turn the frame, so a turned screen there goes to UiAutomation. setprop debug.mobax.mirror 0 before mobax use skips the mirror to try this path.
  • BroadcastReceiver registrations from our Context aren't routed — appCounts cache TTL'd at 4.5 s instead.
  • Most binder lookups go via reflection so the jar compiles against the public SDK. If a new SDK level renames a method, widen the matcher in the relevant helper.

docs.title: adb and the Android SDK
docs.text:
• Two SDKs on one machine (say Android Studio's and the one android info reports) ship different adb versions. Whichever client talks to the other's server kills and restarts it, which drops open connections and can hang a pipeline waiting on output. Point everything at one SDK, or pin MOBILEAX_ADB.
  • A set-but-empty ANDROID_HOME makes android info report an empty SDK path; mobax drops empty ANDROID_HOME / ANDROID_SDK_ROOT before asking it.
  • android emulator start has no -gpu flag; host GPU rendering has to come from hw.gpu.mode=host in the AVD's config.ini, or ForceGpuHost = on in ~/.android/advancedFeatures.ini (Emulators).
  • Running one AVD more than once needs -read-only on every instance, and a read-only emulator refuses snapshot save and load ("Snapshot save is disabled because "-read-only" was specified"). Keep the emulator you reset with snapshots as a single writable instance.
  • After a snapshot load or a reboot done by another tool, the daemon on the device may be gone. mobax and the MCP server start it again on the next call; @N refs from before are refused and the current screen comes back.
  • logcat -t N takes the last N lines before its priority, tag and regex filters, so logcat -t 50 *:E is often empty. mobax logs --level / --tag / --grep / --exclude reads the buffer and keeps the last N matching lines itself.
  • mobax logs --grep is logcat's own regex (ECMAScript, on the device). It has no case-insensitive flag, so -i spells each letter both ways ([aA]); letters at the ends of a class range like [a-z] stay as written. --exclude is plain text, matched on the host.
  • mobax logs --since 5m reads the device's clock, not the host's.
  • mobax logs QUERY takes Android Studio's Logcat filter (package:mine level:WARN -tag:chatty, ~: regex, =: exact, | & ( )) and matches it on the host over logcat -v threadtime -v uid. package: (and --pkg) goes by the entry's uid, so it covers an app's earlier, dead processes and follows it across restarts; package:mine is the app in front when the command starts. A uid several packages share (Settings runs as system, uid 1000, with system_server) is told apart by process name, so there only processes running when the command starts count. On Android 11+ a query limited to packages is narrowed on the device (primary user's uids), so only those lines leave it: logcat --uid on Android 11+, the daemon's logcat_uid (logcat piped through grep) on Android 10 and older. Quote the query as one argument when it has spaces inside a value: 'message:"timed out"'. is:crash is AndroidRuntime errors and native crash lines; age: is the same as --since.

docs.title: Wire reference
docs.text:
The on-device daemon speaks a length-prefixed binary protocol: each frame is uint32 big-endian length + payload (in both directions). Commands are ASCII text, verb [k=v …] style. This document lists every wire verb the daemon dispatches in daemon/core/src/main/kotlin/dev/mobileax/daemon/Server.kt (and Dispatch.kt).

Use these directly via mobax do <wire> or mobax shell (one socket, many commands). ERR:<msg> is returned on failure.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
ping                                                  → pong
ready                                                 → ready (once UiAutomation is connected; `use --instr` waits on it)
info                                                  → "<srcW> <srcH>"
quit                                                  → bye   (daemon exits)

docs.title: Inspect — accessibility tree
docs.text:
dump             [display=N]                          full JSON dump, every window (another display: SDK 30+)
dump_active                                           active window only

A node's bounds are the part of it that shows: cut to its window and to every scrolling ancestor, so a half-hidden row's centre is on screen. A node nothing of which shows keeps the framework's bounds (often cut at one edge, even inverted) and has off: below, above, left or right. A Compose node with no resource id but a testTag reports the tag as rid.

docs.title: Capture — screenshots and streams
docs.text:
screenshot returns one frame; the stream_* verbs hold the socket open and push continuously.

screenshot       [size=N] [q=N] [fmt=jpeg|webp|png] [max=1] [secure_check=1] [rect=L,T,R,B]
stream           [size=N] [q=N] [fps=N]                  JPEG, native by default
stream_h264      [size=N] [max=1] [fps=N] [bitrate=KBPS] [gop=SEC]
stream_tilejpeg  [size=N] [q=N] [tile=N]
keyframe                                                 force IDR on all H.264 streams

size=N = long edge in pixels, default 768. q clamps to [1, 100], default 80. fmt=jpeg is the default and preferred hot path for agents. fmt=webp is available for compact lossy exports, though it may encode slower than JPEG on emulators. fmt=png is intended for debug/export only; Android's PNG encoder is much slower than JPEG. max=1 = native resolution (overrides size). secure_check=1 enables an extra FLAG_SECURE probe for suspiciously small black frames; it is off by default because it shells out to dumpsys window.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
tap         x=NUM y=NUM [display=N]
swipe       x1=NUM y1=NUM x2=NUM y2=NUM [dur=MS] [display=N]
swipe_dir   left|right|up|down [dur=MS] [display=N]                  60% travel from screen centre
pinch       in|out [x=NUM y=NUM] [span=PX] [dur=MS] [display=N]      two fingers together (in) or apart (out)
down        x=NUM y=NUM                                  pointer down (sticks)
move        x=NUM y=NUM
up          x=NUM y=NUM                                  releases the down pointer
scroll      x=NUM y=NUM dy=NUM                           wheel scroll at point
key         NAME                                         e.g. BACK, HOME, ENTER
key         code=N                                       raw KeyEvent code
key         ACCEPT | DISMISS                             answer the dialog on screen (`go accept|dismiss`):
                                                         a permission prompt's first allow/deny button,
                                                         an alert's button1/button2, else (Compose,
                                                         custom) the bottom row of a window smaller
                                                         than the screen: right accepts, left dismisses
key         HIDE_KEYBOARD                                back, only while the soft keyboard is up
                                                         key/scroll take wait=0: don't wait for the
                                                         window to handle it or for animations to
                                                         end (a live viewer; Back in Recents took 5 s)

                                                         (KeyEvents for a password field or a

docs.title: Waits — event-driven, no polling
docs.text:
wait_for_idle      [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=5000]     → ok elapsed=N idle=M | ERR:timeout
                                                         elapsed: ms waited; idle: ms the
                                                         screen had been quiet by then
event_seq                                              → seq=N  (events seen so far)
settle             since=N [first_ms=200] [idle_ms=120] [timeout_ms=1500]
                                                       → ok elapsed=N changed=0|1 | ERR:TIMEOUT
                                                         read event_seq before an action, then
                                                         settle: waits up to first_ms for the
                                                         action's first event, then idle_ms of
                                                         quiet; changed=0 when nothing happened
settle_dump        since=N [first_ms=200] [idle_ms=120] [timeout_ms=1500]
                                                       → ok elapsed=N changed=0|1 moving=0|1
                                                         then a newline and the `dump` JSON
                                                         settle, then the screen once it holds
                                                         still: while an app window reaches past
                                                         the screen's edge (sliding in) it waits
                                                         for the next event, and two dumps 40 ms
                                                         apart must agree; moving=1: never quiet
wait_for_text      text="…" [match=sub|exact] [scope=all|app|active] [timeout_ms=5000]
                                                       → ok x=… y=… w=… h=… elapsed=…
wait_for_activity  n=COMPONENT [timeout_ms=5000]       prefix-matches the package

docs.title: Composites
docs.text:
Tap then await the UI to settle — saves a wire round-trip versus tap + wait_for_idle.

tap_and_dump   x=NUM y=NUM [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=2000]   → dump_active JSON
tap_and_settle x=NUM y=NUM [idle_ms=200] [timeout_ms=2000]   → ok elapsed=N idle=M

docs.title: State — push-mirrored snapshot
docs.text:
ui_watch [min_ms=250] [moves=0|1] keeps the socket and pushes the window tree (the dump payload) each time it changes: {"seq":N,"ev":EVENTS,"dump":{…}}. Driven by accessibility events, not polling; a dump equal to the last one is not sent, frames are at least min_ms apart (floor 50), the last change is always sent, and a slow reader gets only the newest frame. Changes in position only (an animation, a scroll in flight) are held until events have been quiet for 300 ms, then sent once with the resting positions; moves=1 sends them as they happen. Hang up to stop.

state reads a single field from the cached snapshot the daemon maintains via accessibility / lifecycle hooks. state_watch keeps the socket open and pushes a fresh JSON frame on every state change.

state interactive | battery_level | battery_charging | top | procs | device | device_fresh
state_watch                                            chunked JSON frames

docs.title: Node actions — AccessibilityNodeInfo
docs.text:
<selector> is a by: query without the prefix (see By queries below), which also reads the older form: id=com.app:id/x text="Sign in", desc~=menu, class=EditText or a bare EditText. Visible nodes only.

node_click       <selector>
node_long_click  <selector>
node_set_text    <selector> value="STRING"     atomic ACTION_SET_TEXT
node_scroll      <selector> [dir=forward|backward|up|down|left|right]
scroll_forward                                 the biggest list one page on (ERR:scroll-end, ERR:no-scrollable)
toasts           since=SEQ                     toast texts after event SEQ, one per line (empty: none)
node_focus       <selector>
submit           [<selector>]                  ACTION_IME_ENTER on focused
                                               EditText (or matched selector) —
                                               fires the field's IME action
                                               (Search / Go / Send / Done / …)

docs.title: By queries — UiAutomator, live
docs.text:
by: queries run UiAutomator's By (ByEngine) against the live tree, visible nodes only. Options come first; q= takes the rest of the line. The CLI and MCP route any target or selector starting by: here.

by_find q=by:QUERY                                  → {"nodes":[…]} (dump node fields)
by_wait [timeout_ms=N] [gone=1] q=by:QUERY          → ok x= y= elapsed= | ERR:TIMEOUT
by_tap [timeout_ms=N] [nth=N] [long=1] [new_window_ms=N] q=by:QUERY
                                                    → ok x= y= [new_window=true|false]
by_swipe dir=up|down|left|right [pct=0.8] [fling=1] [nth=N] q=by:QUERY
                                                    → ok scroll|swipe|fling [end]
by_pinch in|out [pct=0.8] [nth=N] q=by:QUERY        → ok pinch in|out
by_drag to=X,Y [speed=N] [nth=N] q=by:QUERY         → ok drag X,Y -> X,Y

QUERY: space-separated terms, all of which hold. text=V (also ~= contains, ^=, $=, =/re/i) for text, desc, hint, res, class, pkg; res=title and class=Button match any package's. Flags clickable, checked, !enabled, …; has(Q) child(Q) parent(Q) in(Q); depth=N; window(pkg=… title~=… type=app|ime|system|overlay active focused display=N). A value with spaces goes in "quotes". dir on by_swipe is the finger's: a scrollable element scrolls (the content moves the other way) and says end when nothing is left.

docs.title: XPath queries — Appium's document, on the device (experimental)
docs.text:
Not advertised in the README, usage or MCP instructions: kept for people bringing Appium locators, and may change or go.

xpath: queries (XPathEngine) build the screen as Appium's UiAutomator2 server shows it — elements named after the class under hierarchy, with index package class text resource-id checkable checked clickable enabled focusable focused long-clickable password scrollable selected displayed content-desc bounds (plus hint, state-description) — and evaluate the XPath there, so Appium Inspector's XPaths work. bounds are the visible ones; a node nothing of which shows has off. A Compose testTag is the resource-id when there is none. XPath 1.0 (Android's engine) plus matches(s, re[, flags]), lower-case, upper-case, ends-with. Class names that aren't XML names get _ for the offending characters (@class is exact). The CLI and MCP route xpath: targets for find, wait and tap here; tap scrolls toward an off node as it does for any other.

xpath_find [scope=app|all] q=XPATH                       → {"nodes":[…],"ms":N,"build_ms":N}
                                                           | {"value":"…"} (count(), string(), …)
xpath_wait [scope=app|all] [timeout_ms=N] [gone=1] q=XPATH → ok x= y= elapsed= | ERR:TIMEOUT

scope=app (default): the app's windows, the one on top first; all: every window. xpath_wait rechecks on accessibility events and ignores nodes marked off.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
pm_list   [3] [s]                       3 = third-party only, s = system only
pm_path   PKG
pm_uninstall PKG
pm_grant  PKG PERM
pm_revoke PKG PERM

docs.title: User-data providers
docs.text:
Reach ContentProviders directly via IContentProvider.query over getContentProviderExternal — no installed app, no pm grant needed. shell UID carries the read permission for all four authorities by default on AOSP / stock Pixel. Response is NDJSON: line 1 = JSON array of column names, then one JSON-array row per line.

sms       [type=inbox|sent|all] [limit=N]      content://sms[/inbox|/sent]
calls     [type=in|out|missed|all] [limit=N]   content://call_log/calls
contacts  [limit=N]                            content://com.android.contacts/contacts
calendar  [from=MS] [to=MS] [limit=N]          content://com.android.calendar/instances/when/<from>/<to>

clip_get                                       → current primary clip text
clip_set <text>                                → "ok" | "ERR:…"  (everything after the space is the literal text)
clip_watch [interval_ms=500]                   → chunked stream, one frame per clipboard change

am_force_stop  PKG

docs.text:
pull streams [len][chunk]…[len=0] back. push expects the same shape from the client after the header.

pull   path=PATH                                       → chunked stream
push   path=PATH size=N [mode=0NNN]                    client streams chunks → ok | ERR

settings_put NS KEY VALUE

docs.text:
dumpsys SERVICE [ARGS…]                                chunked stream
logcat  [ARGS…]                                        chunked stream
logcat_uid UID[,UID…] [ARGS…]                         logcat's lines of those uids (ARGS has `-v uid`; Android ≤10, no --uid)

docs.title: Quoting and escaping
docs.text:
• Arguments are split on ASCII whitespace.
  • "..." quoted strings are honoured for text="…" / value="…" and similar — useful when the value contains spaces or =.
  • Selectors are passed as-is; quote any embedded whitespace.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Every failure path returns a single frame whose payload starts with ERR: followed by a short tag (e.g. ERR:tap_and_dump-needs-x-y). Streamed responses send the ERR: frame then the len=0 terminator.

docs.title: UiDevice/By 셀렉터 스터디 (main, app_process 데몬)
docs.text: 날짜: 2026-11-03 · 브랜치: study/uidevice-selector (origin/main c05f457에서) · 기기: 에뮬레이터 Medium_Phone SDK 36

docs.title: 질문
docs.text:
1. 설치 없이 shell uid로 도는 main의 app_process 데몬에서 공식 androidx.test.uiautomator(UiDevice, By, UiObject2)를 쓸 수 있는가?
  2. 쓸 수 있다면, 지금의 호스트 쪽 셀렉터(mobax-core/src/selector.rs, dump JSON 위에서 매칭)를 By 기반으로 바꿀 이유가 있는가?

docs.title: 방법 (스파이크, 병합하지 않음)
docs.text:
• build.gradle.kts에 androidx.test.uiautomator:uiautomator:2.4.0을 추가했다. 소스를 복사하지 않고 공식 라이브러리를 그대로 썼다.
  • ByStudy.kt: Instrumentation을 상속한 shim이 getUiAutomation()/getUiAutomation(flags)에서 데몬이 이미 연결한 UiAutomation을, getContext()/getTargetContext()에서 시스템 컨텍스트를 돌려준다. Configurator.uiAutomationFlags는 데몬과 같은 값(FLAG_DONT_SUPPRESS_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES)으로 맞췄다. 이 shim을 UiDevice.getInstance(shim)에 넘긴다.
  • 임시 wire verb by_find KEY=VALUE는 UiDevice.findObjects(By…)를 실행하고 개수, 첫 결과의 visibleBounds, 기기 안 소요 시간을 돌려준다.
  • 같은 화면에서 mobax find '<호스트 셀렉터>'와 비교했다. 측정 스크립트는 각 질의를 10회 실행했다.

docs.title: 1. 실현 가능성: 된다
docs.text:
• shim Instrumentation만으로 공식 uiautomator 2.4.0이 app_process 데몬 안에서 동작했다. InstrumentationRegistry, 실제 instrumentation, 소스 복사가 모두 필요 없었다.
  • UiDevice 초기화는 27ms, APK 크기는 +36KB였다(194KB → 231KB, R8 적용 후).
  • 시험한 By는 text, textContains, text(Pattern), res, clazz, clickable, hasDescendant, desc이고 모두 정상 응답했다.
  • 단서: shim은 UiDevice가 Instrumentation에서 위 네 메서드만 쓴다는 데 기대고 있다. SDK 36에서만 확인했다. UiDevice의 다른 기능(executeShellCommand, 화면 회전, pressKeyCode)은 시험하지 않았다.

docs.title: 2. 속도: 비긴다
docs.text:
질의 (설정 첫 화면) By 기기 안 시간(중앙값) by_find 전체 왕복 호스트 find 전체 왕복 text=네트워크 및 인터넷 4.3ms 181ms 165ms textContains=네트워크 4.7ms 165ms 180ms res=android:id/title 4.1ms 168ms 183ms clickable 4.0ms 162ms 165ms
  • 비교 기준: 호스트 방식의 기기 쪽 비용은 dump_active 한 번이고, 같은 화면에서 중앙값 3.6ms였다(mobax dev bench). 전체 왕복은 둘 다 CLI 프로세스 시작이 대부분이다.
  • 앱 서랍(노드 51개)에서도 By.clickable 4.1~4.9ms, dump_active 3.4ms로 차이가 없었다.
  • 예외: 화면을 막 연 직후 첫 By 조회는 448ms가 걸렸다. live 트리를 처음 훑으며 접근성 캐시를 채우기 때문으로 보인다. dump 쪽은 전환 대기(waitOutTransition)를 거친다.

docs.title: 3. 의미 차이
docs.text: 항목 By / UiObject2 지금 셀렉터 보이지 않는 노드 기본으로 제외(보이는 노드만) 기본으로 포함, --visible/:visible로 걸러야 함. 설정 화면 clickable이 10 대 21이었고, 차이 11개는 스크롤 아래 화면 밖 항목(bounds가 화면 밖이거나 뒤집힘) 텍스트 정확·부분·접두·접미, Pattern(정규식, 대소문자 무시 가능) 정확·부분·접두·접미. 정규식 없음, 대소문자 구분 구조 hasChild/hasDescendant/hasParent/hasAncestor, depth :in(SEL)(조상). :has() 없음 hasDescendant 결과 그 후손을 가진 모든 조상이 매치(예: 12개) 해당 없음 위치 관계 없음 :below, :right-of, :near 대상 조회 시점의 live 트리. 결과 객체가 금방 낡을 수 있음(StaleObjectException) 에이전트가 본 그 dump(ui의 @N과 같은 스냅샷) 문자열 문법 없음(코드 API) CSS/Playwright 계열 문자열

docs.title: 판단
docs.text:
• By로 매칭 엔진을 바꿀 이유는 약하다.
  • 속도 이득이 없다.
  • CLI, MCP, 스크립트에는 문자열 문법이 여전히 필요해서 파서는 그대로 남는다.
  • 에이전트에게 쓸모가 큰 위치 관계(:below, :near)를 잃는다.
  • live 조회는 에이전트가 본 스냅샷과 어긋날 수 있다.
  • By에서 가져올 것:
  • 보이는 노드만 기본으로. 화면 밖 노드를 누르거나 세는 실수를 막는다. 기존 스크립트의 결과가 바뀌는 의미 변경이라 결정이 필요하다. 예를 들어 --all-nodes로 예전 동작을 남길 수 있다.
  • 정규식과 대소문자 무시. Pattern에 해당하는 연산자.
  • :has(SEL). hasDescendant에 해당한다. 가장 가까운 조상만 고르는 규칙을 함께 정해야 한다(By처럼 모든 조상이 매치되면 모호해진다).
  • UiDevice를 다른 용도로 쓰는 길은 열려 있다. main에서도 shim으로 동작하니, 필요해지면 설치 없이 들여올 수 있다. 예를 들어 UiObject2.scrollUntil/fling 같은 스크롤 동작이다.
  • 셀렉터 파서의 기존 버그(따옴표 안의 ]·(·연산자 문자, 모르는 속성 이름의 무음 실패, :below가 거리순이 아님, 관계 조건의 반복 탐색)는 이 결정과 별개로 고칠 일이다.

docs.title: 가상 디스플레이 없이 화면 캡처하기
docs.text: 날짜: 2026-11-04 · 브랜치: spike/capture (daemon/dual-target에서; 측정용 CapSpike.kt와 함께 지움, 결론은 DisplayCapture.kt로 들어감) · 기기: 에뮬레이터 Medium_Phone SDK 36, headless, -gpu host

docs.title: 질문
docs.text: instrumentation 데몬(app uid, shell 권한 위임)에서 상주 미러(VirtualDisplay) 없이 필요할 때만 캡처한다면, UiAutomation.takeScreenshot()보다 빠른 길이 있는가?

docs.title: 방법
docs.text:
임시 wire 명령 cap_spike mode=ua|wm|a11y [scale] [crop] n=10(CapSpike.kt)으로 세 경로를 jar와 APK 두 빌드에서 10회씩 쟀다. 캡처는 버퍼가 데몬 손에 들어오기까지, 인코딩은 일반 Bitmap 변환과 JPEG(품질 80)까지다.

  • ua: UiAutomation.takeScreenshot(). UiAutomationConnection이 있는 프로세스가 캡처해 일반 Bitmap으로 복사한 뒤 바인더로 넘긴다. 축소와 자르기는 CPU에서 한다.
  • wm: 숨겨진 IWindowManager.captureDisplay(displayId, CaptureArgs, ScreenCaptureListener)(34+). frameScale과 sourceCrop이 합성 단계에서 적용되고, HardwareBuffer가 데몬으로 온다. WMS는 READ_FRAME_BUFFER를 checkCallingPermission으로 검사한다.
  • a11y: UiAutomation의 접근성 연결(IAccessibilityServiceConnection.takeScreenshot(displayId, RemoteCallback), 30+).

docs.title: 결과 (중앙값, ms)
docs.text:
경로 출력 jar 캡처 / 인코딩 APK 캡처 / 인코딩 ua 1080×2400 58.5 / 20.5 54.3 / 11.7 ua 축소 383×852 58.4 / 5.4 54.8 / 3.5 wm 1080×2400 33.4 / 41.7 33.7 / 32.7 wm 축소 383×852 11.7 / 6.1 11.3 / 6.0 wm 자르기 1080×400 12.7 / 8.5 12.6 / 6.4 a11y 응답 없음 응답 없음
  • wm은 APK에서도 된다. shell 권한 위임이 WMS의 Java 권한 검사에 적용된다.
  • 미리보기 크기(383×852)에서 wm은 약 17ms이고, ua는 약 60ms다. ua는 축소해도 캡처 비용이 줄지 않는다. 전체 해상도를 만들어 복사하고 넘긴 뒤에 줄이기 때문이다.
  • 전체 해상도에서는 wm의 인코딩이 더 느리다. HARDWARE Bitmap을 일반 Bitmap으로 읽어 오는 비용(약 30ms)이 여기에 들어간다. 캡처와 인코딩을 합치면 두 경로가 비슷하다(75 대 66~79).
  • a11y는 콜백이 오지 않는다. 서비스의 screenshot 권한(capability)을 검사하는 단계에서 막히는 것으로 보인다. oneway 호출이라 예외가 돌아오지 않는다. UiAutomation에는 이 권한이 없고, 창 단위 캡처(takeScreenshotOfWindow)도 같은 검사를 거치므로 이 길은 막혀 있다.

docs.title: 판단
docs.text:
• 상주 미러 없이 필요할 때 찍는 정지 화면(see, 요소 스크린샷) 은 wm 경로가 맞다. 축소와 자르기를 합성 단계로 넘기는 것이 핵심이다. 요소 스크린샷은 sourceCrop으로 그 요소만 합성하면 된다.
  • 상주 미러는 768px 기준 약 3ms(SDK 29/33 측정)로 더 빠르다. 다만 미러를 계속 띄워 두는 비용이 든다. 스트림에는 계속 VirtualDisplay를 쓴다.
  • 33 이하에는 IWindowManager.captureDisplay가 없다. 31–33에서는 SurfaceControl.captureDisplay를 써야 하고, 아직 시험하지 않았다.
  • 다음: see가 미러가 없을 때 wm 경로를 먼저 쓰게 하고 SDK 31–35에서 확인한다. 화면이 안 바뀌었을 때(이벤트 번호가 같을 때) 다시 찍지 않는 캐시도 붙인다.

docs.title: 숨겨진 API 점검: 공식 API로 바꿀 수 있는 것
docs.text:
날짜: 2026-11-04 · 브랜치: daemon/public-apis (main 7cc0926에서)

appium-uiautomator2-server는 instrumentation 프로세스 안에서 공식 API만 쓴다. main 데몬(app_process, shell uid)은 설치가 없고 실시간 화면이 가벼운 대신 숨겨진 API에 기대는 곳이 있다. 프로세스 모델은 유지하고, 공식 대안이 있는 호출만 바꾼다. 대안이 없는 호출은 실패할 때의 대체 경로와 버전별 확인으로 다룬다.

docs.title: A. app_process라서 피할 수 없는 것 (유지)
docs.text:
ActivityThread 없이 Context와 UiAutomation을 직접 만드는 부분이다. instrumentation이라면 프레임워크가 해 주는 일이다.

호출 위치 용도 ActivityThread.systemMain · getSystemContext · makeApplication · mInitialApplication Binders, Main Context, Application UiAutomationConnection · IUiAutomationConnection.connect Main UiAutomation 연결 VMRuntime.setHiddenApiExemptions Main 숨겨진 API 접근 ServiceManager.getService · I*$Stub.asInterface Binders 시스템 서비스 바인더 DdmHandleAppName, BaseBundle.setShouldDefuse, Looper.setSlowLogThresholdMs Main 디버거 이름, 진단

docs.title: B. 공식 대안이 있는 것 (바꿈)
docs.text: 호출 위치 공식 대안 API IWindowManager.freezeRotation Wm UiAutomation.setRotation (instrumentation 브랜치 8218d28에서 검증) 18 IPackageManager/IPermissionManager.grant·revokeRuntimePermission Pm UiAutomation.grantRuntimePermission · revokeRuntimePermission 28 IPowerManager.isInteractive State PowerManager.isInteractive() 20 DisplayManagerGlobal.getRealDisplay Screenshot DisplayManager.getDisplay 17

docs.title: C. 공식 대안이 없거나 부족한 것 (유지, 대체 경로 확인)
docs.text: 호출 위치 이유 지금의 대체 SurfaceControl.createDisplay 외 MirrorDisplay 10~13 미러: 공식 길은 MediaProjection(앱·알림 필요) 실패하면 takeScreenshot IActivityTaskManager.startActivityAsUser Am 공식 Context.startActivity는 백그라운드 실행 제한과 결과 코드(result=2/3)가 없음 없음 IActivityManager.forceStopPackage Am ActivityManager.forceStopPackage는 SystemApi 없음 (am force-stop과 같은 바인더) 3-인자 injectInputEvent Input 애니메이션 대기를 끄는 길이 숨겨진 쪽뿐 2-인자 공개 메서드 InputEvent.setDisplayId Input 다른 디스플레이로 입력 없음 (오류로 알림) SystemProperties.get/set Props, State 공개 API 없음 없음 (수십 년 안정) IClipboard Clipboard 공개 ClipboardManager는 백그라운드 읽기가 막힘 없음 ContentProviderHolder.provider, AttributionSource Providers, SettingsDirect ContentResolver 없이 프로바이더 직접 호출 없음 SessionParams.installFlags Installer 설치 플래그 일부는 SystemApi setRequireUserAction은 31+ 공개 IIntentSender Transfers 앱 없이 설치 결과 받기 없음 AssetManager() + addAssetPath Manifest 공개 getResourcesForApplication(...).assets에는 프레임워크 리소스도 있어 AndroidManifest.xml이 어느 APK 것인지(쿠키) 정해지지 않음 없음

docs.title: 다음
docs.text:
• B를 바꾸고 SDK 29, 33, 36에서 확인한다.
  • C는 버전별 스모크 테스트(미러, 실행, 입력, 권한, 설치)로 감시한다.

docs.title: 데몬 단일 루퍼 + Gradle 빌드 Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: on-device 데몬을 MainLooper 하나 + 작은 Work 풀 구조의 Kotlin 코루틴 모델로 바꾸고, Gradle이 build/hs.jar를 만드는 정식 빌드가 되게 한다. 와이어 프로토콜은 바이트 단위로 유지.

Architecture: Looper.loop()를 도는 main 스레드가 MessageQueue.addOnFileDescriptorEventListener(epoll)로 소켓·파이프를 감시하고, 연결마다 Dispatchers.Main 위의 코루틴 하나가 readFrame → dispatch → respond를 suspend로 처리한다. CPU/장시간 binder 작업만 Work 디스패처로 보낸다. 중간 단계에서는 아직 포팅 안 된 블로킹 Java 핸들러를 Legacy 디스패처 + 블로킹 스트림 어댑터로 돌려 매 태스크마다 jar가 동작하게 하고, 마지막에 Legacy를 제거한다.

Tech Stack: Kotlin 2.2.21 (JVM target 17), kotlinx-coroutines-core/android (최신 안정 1.10.x), Gradle(Kotlin DSL, 기존 wrapper), SDK R8(build-tools/36.0.0/lib/d8.jar), JUnit5 + kotlinx-coroutines-test (JVM 단위 테스트), Python 3 (scripts/wire-smoke.py, 기기 통합 테스트), AVD Medium_Phone(API 36).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-daemon-looper-gradle-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• 와이어 프로토콜(docs/wire.md): verb, 인자, 응답 바이트, uint32 BE length + payload 프레이밍, ERR: 문자열, 스트림 len=0 종결자, __exit__ N 트레일러 — 전부 기존과 동일. MAX_CMD = 256, 위반 시 BAD_ARG:bad-length:<len> 후 연결 종료.
  • 엔트리: dev.handsets.daemon.Main.main(String[]), --port=N(기본 9008), 127.0.0.1 바인드, backlog 8, SO_REUSEADDR, TCP_NODELAY. stdout에 hsd listening on 127.0.0.1:<port> 와 hsd ready (sdk=<N>) 출력 유지.
  • 산출물: build/hs.jar (dex만), --min-api 28, R8 --release. 크기 목표: 기준 jar 대비 +300KB 이내, 초과 시 보고.
  • R8: SDK build-tools/<ver>/lib/d8.jar의 com.android.tools.r8.R8를 JavaExec로 실행. 기본 build-tools 36.0.0, -PbuildTools=로 변경.
  • 루퍼(main)에서 금지: 덤프, 인코딩, Thread.sleep, 블로킹 소켓/파이프 I/O, 상한 없는 binder 호출. 애매하면 Work.
  • 스레드 최종 상태: main + Work 풀(min(4, availableProcessors)) (+ 프레임워크 binder/MediaCodec 스레드). hs-ua는 main looper 시도가 실패할 때만 예외로 허용하고 보고.
  • 이미지/상태 스트림(stream, stream_tilejpeg, state_watch, clip_watch)은 최신 프레임만 유지. stream_h264는 공유 전까지 프레임 무손실 + 연결별 backpressure.
  • 호스트 코드(handsets-cli, handsets-tui, handsets-viewer, bindings/) 수정 금지.
  • 검증 기기: AVD Medium_Phone (API 36, x86_64) 하나. adb: E:\packages\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. TCP 단편화: 명령 프레임의 4바이트 길이/페이로드가 여러 read로 쪼개져 도착 → 하나의 명령으로 정상 처리. (Task 3 ConnTest.fragmentedFrame)
  2. 스트림 중 클라이언트 강제 종료: stream*/state_watch/logcat/shell 중 소켓이 끊김 → 구독 해제, 서브프로세스 kill, 인코더/VirtualDisplay 해제, 다른 연결 영향 없음. (Task 3 ConnTest.cancelOnEof, Task 9 smoke disconnect_cleanup)
  3. 느린/읽지 않는 클라이언트: 스트림을 열고 읽지 않는 클라이언트가 있어도 다른 연결의 ping p95 < 50ms. (Task 3 ConnTest.latestOnlyReplaces, Task 8 smoke slow_client)
  4. 설치 중 업로드 중단: install size=N 후 N바이트를 다 보내기 전에 끊김 → 세션 abandon, 데몬 정상. (Task 6 smoke install_truncated)
  5. UTF-8 / 경계 길이 명령: CJK clip_set, text, 길이 정확히 256/257 프레임 → 기존과 같은 응답. (Task 4 DispatchTest.cjkAndLengthBounds, smoke 케이스)

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
새 Kotlin 파일 (src/dev/handsets/daemon/, 패키지 dev.handsets.daemon):

파일 책임 Loop.kt Main/Work/Legacy 디스패처, 루트 scope, onMain {} 헬퍼 IoLoop.kt IoLoop 인터페이스 + MessageQueueIoLoop(Android), fd 획득 Fds Conn.kt 비블로킹 연결: suspend 읽기, 출력 큐(backpressure / latest-only), 종료 HsServer.kt accept 루프, 연결별 코루틴 Dispatch.kt verb 디스패치 (기존 Server.handle switch + run* 포팅) Args.kt 기존 Server의 순수 파싱 헬퍼(strArg, longArg, positional, parseInputArgs, …) 포팅 Main.kt 엔트리, 초기화 순서, Looper.loop() (기존 Main.java 대체) Waits.kt UiEvents + WaitRegistry 대체 (suspend) StateRefresher.kt Debouncer + State 리프레시/구독 fan-out ProcStream.kt 서브프로세스 stdout을 IoLoop로 읽어 청크 프레임 전송 Streams.kt stream/stream_tilejpeg/stream_h264/state_watch/clip_watch 세션 LegacyStreams.kt 임시: Conn ↔ 블로킹 DataInputStream/DataOutputStream 어댑터 (Task 9에서 삭제)

docs.title: Task 3: 이벤트 루프 코어 (Loop, IoLoop, Conn)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: src/dev/handsets/daemon/Loop.kt, IoLoop.kt, Conn.kt - Test: test/dev/handsets/daemon/ConnTest.kt, test/dev/handsets/daemon/SelectorIoLoop.kt(테스트용 IoLoop 구현)

Interfaces: - Produces: - Loop.kt: object Loop { val Main: CoroutineDispatcher; val Work: CoroutineDispatcher; val Legacy: CoroutineDispatcher; val scope: CoroutineScope; fun init(main: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Main.immediate) } — Work = 고정 min(4, cpu) 데몬 스레드 풀(hs-work-N) .asCoroutineDispatcher(), Legacy = 캐시드 풀(hs-legacy-N, Task 9에서 제거). scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Main + CoroutineExceptionHandler{ 로그 }). init이 Dispatchers.Main 해석 실패 시 Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).asCoroutineDispatcher("hs-main")로 대체하고 어느 쪽인지 stderr에 hsd dispatcher: main=<kind> 출력. - IoLoop.kt: interface IoLoop { fun watch(fd: FileDescriptor, events: Int, cb: (fd: FileDescriptor, events: Int) -> Int); fun unwatch(fd: FileDescriptor) } (events/반환값 의미는 MessageQueue.OnFileDescriptorEventListener와 동일: EVENT_INPUT=1, EVENT_OUTPUT=2, EVENT_ERROR=4, 0 반환 = 해제). class MessageQueueIoLoop(queue: MessageQueue) : IoLoop. object Fds { fun of(ch: SelectableChannel): FileDescriptor } — Android SocketChannelImpl/ServerSocketChannelImpl의 getFD()를 리플렉션으로 호출. - Conn.kt: class Conn(ch: SocketChannel, io: IoLoop) { suspend fun readInt(): Int; suspend fun readFully(n: Int): ByteArray; suspend fun readChunk(max: Int): ByteArray? /* null=EOF */; suspend fun send(payload: ByteArray) /* 프레임(len+payload) 큐잉, 큐 바이트 > OUT_LIMIT(4 MiB)이면 drain까지 suspend */; suspend fun sendRaw(bytes: ByteArray) /* 길이 접두 없이 */; fun sendLatest(slot: Int, payload: ByteArray) /* 같은 slot의 아직 안 나간 프레임을 교체 */; suspend fun flush(); val job: Job /* EOF/에러/close 시 cancel */; fun close() }. 읽기 EOF는 EOFException을 던진다.

  • [ ] Step 1: 실패하는 테스트 작성 — ConnTest (JVM, SelectorIoLoop가 별도 스레드에서 java.nio.channels.Selector로 IoLoop 계약을 흉내, 디스패처는 단일 스레드 executor):
  • fragmentedFrame: 클라이언트가 [0,0,0,4]를 2바이트씩, "ping"을 1바이트씩 보냄 → readInt()==4, String(readFully(4))=="ping".
  • sendFramesInOrder: send("a"), send("bb") → 클라이언트가 00000001 61 00000002 6262 수신.
  • backpressureSuspends: 클라이언트가 읽지 않을 때 send를 반복하면 누적 큐 바이트가 OUT_LIMIT+최대 프레임 1개를 넘지 않음(초과 시점에 suspend 확인 — withTimeoutOrNull(200){ send(big) } == null).
  • latestOnlyReplaces: 읽지 않는 클라이언트에 sendLatest(0, f1..f50) → 클라이언트가 읽기 시작하면 받은 프레임 수 ≤ 3 이고 마지막이 f50.
  • cancelOnEof: 클라이언트 close → conn.job.isCancelled 가 1초 내 true, 진행 중 readInt()는 EOFException/취소로 끝남.
  • [ ] Step 2: Run: ./gradlew test --tests '*ConnTest*' — Expected: FAIL (클래스 없음).
  • [ ] Step 3: Loop.kt, IoLoop.kt, Conn.kt 구현. Conn은 읽기 대기 시 EVENT_INPUT, 출력 큐가 비어 있지 않을 때만 EVENT_OUTPUT을 watch(쓰기 가능할 때마다 non-blocking write). 소켓은 configureBlocking(false), TCP_NODELAY.
  • [ ] Step 4: Run: ./gradlew test --tests '*ConnTest*' — Expected: PASS.
  • [ ] Step 5: Commit — daemon: looper io core (IoLoop, Conn, dispatchers)

docs.text:
Files: - Create: HsServer.kt, Dispatch.kt, Args.kt, Main.kt, LegacyStreams.kt - Delete: Server.java, Main.java - Modify: Binders.java(prepareMainLooper 호출 제거 — Main이 담당), Screenshot.java(미러 HandlerThread는 그대로; Task 8에서 처리) - Test: test/dev/handsets/daemon/ArgsTest.kt, test/dev/handsets/daemon/DispatchTest.kt

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 3 Loop, IoLoop, Fds, Conn. - Produces: - class HsServer(port: Int, io: IoLoop, dispatch: Dispatch) { fun start() } — ServerSocketChannel non-blocking, accept마다 Loop.scope.launch { dispatch.session(conn) }. - class Dispatch(h: Handlers) { suspend fun session(c: Conn) } — 기존 Server.handle 루프와 같은 순서: readInt → 길이 검사 → readFully → UTF-8 → trim → head 분기. 스트림 verb 후 return(연결 종료) / 청크 verb 후 continue 의미 유지. - class Handlers (Kotlin, 기존 Server.Handlers 필드 동일 이름, lateinit var). - Args.kt: 기존 Server private static 헬퍼를 이름 그대로 top-level internal fun으로 (strArg, strArgOr, longArg, extractKey, removeKey, positional, positionalPair, afterHead, parseInputArgs, parseScreenshotArgs, parseFileArgs, parseAmArgs, clampQuality, utf8, errBytes, textSelector). parseScreenshotArgs/textSelector처럼 android 타입을 쓰는 것은 별도 파일로 분리 가능. - LegacyStreams.kt: fun Conn.blockingOut(): DataOutputStream (쓰기 → runBlocking(Loop.Main)이 아닌 Loop.scope.launch{ sendRaw } + 용량 세마포어로 Legacy 스레드만 블로킹), fun Conn.blockingIn(): DataInputStream (Legacy 스레드에서 runBlocking { readChunk }). 아직 포팅 안 된 핸들러(Files.pull/push, Installer, Dumpsys, Logcat, ShellExec, Lifecycle, Clipboard.watch, Streamer, TileStreamer, H264Streamer, state_watch, waits)는 withContext(Loop.Legacy) { 기존 Java 호출(blockingIn/Out) }. byte[]를 반환하는 동기 핸들러 중 덤프·provider·pm_list·notifications·screenshot·deeplinks·location·settings는 withContext(Loop.Work), 나머지 짧은 것(ping, info, getprop, keyframe, wm_info, state <field> 캐시 읽기)은 main에서 직접. - Main.kt: object Main { @JvmStatic fun main(args: Array<String>) } 순서: hidden-API 해제 → Looper.prepareMainLooper() → Loop.init() → HsServer.start()(listening 출력) → Loop.scope.launch { initDaemon() } → Looper.loop(). initDaemon: withContext(Work){ UiAutomation(mainLooper, conn) 생성 + connectWithRetry + setServiceInfo/flags + setRunAsMonkey } → main에서 핸들러 생성 → warmup(launch(Work){ dumper.dumpActive() }) → hsd ready (sdk=N) 출력 → ready.complete(Unit). Dispatch.session은 ping/quit 외 verb 처리 전 ready.await(). UA connect가 5초 내 실패/교착이면 hs-ua HandlerThread looper로 재생성하고 stderr hsd ua-looper=thread(성공 시 =main) 출력. 셧다운 훅(UA disconnect) 유지. quit은 bye 전송·flush 후 exitProcess(0).

DispatchTest.cjkAndLengthBounds: 가짜 Handlers로 Dispatch.session을 SelectorIoLoop 위에서 돌려 len=0→ERR:BAD_ARG:bad-length:0+종료, len=257→ERR:BAD_ARG:bad-length:257+종료, len=256 정상 처리, ping→pong. docs.title: Task 5: UI 이벤트·대기·State·Input을 main으로
docs.text:
Files: - Create: Waits.kt, StateRefresher.kt, Input.kt(기존 Input.java 대체) - Delete: UiEvents.java, WaitRegistry.java, Input.java - Modify: State.java(refresher 스레드·HandlerThread 3개·ensureRefresher/markDirty/dirtyLock 제거, 리스너 등록을 주입받은 main Handler로; computeDevice()는 그대로 두고 package-private로), Dispatch.kt(waits/tap_and_*/state/state_watch/input을 Legacy에서 suspend 호출로) - Test: test/dev/handsets/daemon/WaitsTest.kt, test/dev/handsets/daemon/DebouncerTest.kt

Interfaces: - Consumes: Loop, Conn.sendLatest. - Produces: - class Waits(clock: () -> Long = SystemClock::uptimeMillis) { fun onEvent(type: Int); fun touch(); suspend fun awaitIdle(idleMs: Long, timeoutMs: Long): Long /* -1=timeout */; suspend fun awaitPredicate(timeoutMs: Long, check: suspend () -> Boolean): Long /* 이벤트마다 재평가, -1=timeout */ ; fun subscribe(c: (AccessibilityEventType: Int) -> Unit) } — UiAutomation.setOnAccessibilityEventListener는 Main.kt가 Waits.onEvent(ev.eventType)로 연결 (UA 콜백 스레드가 main이 아니면 Handler(main).post). wait_for_text의 노드 검색 predicate는 withContext(Work). - class Debouncer(scope: CoroutineScope, debounceMs: Long, heartbeatMs: Long, action: suspend () -> Unit) { fun mark() } — mark()마다 debounce 재시작, 마지막 실행 후 heartbeatMs 경과 시에도 실행. DEBOUNCE_MS/HEARTBEAT_MS 값은 State.java 기존 상수 그대로. - class StateRefresher(state: State, scope) { fun ensureStarted(); fun subscribe(l: (ByteArray) -> Unit); fun unsubscribe(l) ; fun deviceFresh(): suspend ByteArray } — action = withContext(Work){ state.computeDevice() } → main에서 캐시 저장 + 구독자 호출. - Input.kt: class Input(ua: UiAutomation) 같은 메서드 이름, swipe/text/keyPress 등 시간 간격이 있는 것은 suspend(delay), injectInputEvent는 withContext(Work). - [ ] Step 1: 실패하는 테스트 (kotlinx-coroutines-test runTest, 가상 시간, 가상 clock = testScheduler.currentTime): - WaitsTest.idleReturnsAfterQuiet: touch() 후 awaitIdle(200, 5000) → 가상 시간 200ms에 반환값 ≥200. - WaitsTest.eventsPostponeIdle: 100ms마다 onEvent 5회 → 반환 시각 = 마지막 이벤트 + 200. - WaitsTest.idleTimeout: 50ms마다 이벤트 계속 → awaitIdle(200, 1000) == -1L, 가상 1000ms에 반환. - WaitsTest.predicateRecheckedOnEvent: check가 3번째 이벤트 후 true → 그 시각의 경과 반환. - DebouncerTest.coalesces: 30ms 간격 mark() 5회 → action 1회, 마지막 mark + debounce 시각. - DebouncerTest.heartbeat: mark 없이 heartbeatMs * 2 경과 → action 2회. - [ ] Step 2: Run: ./gradlew test --tests '*WaitsTest*' --tests '*DebouncerTest*' — FAIL. - [ ] Step 3: 구현 + State.java 정리 + Dispatch 연결(state_watch는 StateRefresher.subscribe { conn.sendLatest(0, it) }, 연결 job 종료 시 unsubscribe). - [ ] Step 4: Run: ./gradlew test — PASS. - [ ] Step 5: 기기 패리티 — Task 4 Step 5와 같은 명령(smoke-t5.json). Expected: diff exit 0, parallel_ping_during_wait true. - [ ] Step 6: Commit — daemon: event-driven waits, state refresh and input on main looper

docs.title: 데몬 instrumentation 이동 — 구현 계획
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: 데몬을 app_process에서 설치된 APK의 instrumentation 프로세스(am instrument -w)로 옮긴다. UiAutomation은 공식 API로 얻고, monkey는 정식으로 켠다. 모든 verb의 동작은 유지한다.

Architecture: - 같은 APK(dev.mobileax.daemon)에 androidx.test.runner.MonitoringInstrumentation(AndroidJUnitRunner의 부모) 서브클래스를 둔다. AMS가 fork한 프로세스의 main looper 위에서 지금의 서버·코루틴 구조를 그대로 돌린다. - instrumentation, context, 인자는 InstrumentationRegistry로 얻는다. UiAutomation은 UiDevice와 같은 인스턴스를 쓴다. 데몬 경로 중 androidx.test로 바꿔도 결과와 성능이 같은 곳은 바꾼다(spec 5.1). - shell 권한이 필요한 일은 두 갈래로 처리한다. 권한 검사는 adoptShellPermissionIdentity()로 통과하고, shell uid 자체가 필요한 일은 executeShellCommand*(shell uid로 실행)로 넘긴다. - 호스트 쪽은 기동과 정리 경로만 바뀐다. 기존 jar push + app_process 대신 APK 설치 + am instrument를 쓴다.

Tech Stack: Kotlin(데몬, AGP, kotlinx-coroutines, androidx.test runner/monitor/uiautomator), Rust std-only(CLI), adb, GitHub Actions

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-daemon-instrumentation-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• minSdk = 29(최종 검토 뒤 사용자 결정으로 31에서 낮춤, spec 3절), compileSdk = 36, targetSdk = 36.
  • 패키지 dev.mobileax.daemon, 소켓 이름 mobaxd_<port>(abstract)는 그대로 둔다. 와이어 프로토콜(docs/wire.md)은 바뀌지 않는다.
  • 릴리즈 APK도 signingConfigs.debug로 서명한다. 키 파일과 CI 시크릿은 쓰지 않는다.
  • app_process 기동 경로는 남기지 않는다(전체 이동).
  • 데몬은 기기당 하나다. 다른 --port로 use하면 오류를 낸다. 메시지에는 mobax drop 후 다시 하라는 안내를 넣는다.
  • CLI는 third-party 의존성 없이 std만 쓴다(mobax-cli/Cargo.toml 주석).
  • 데몬 의존성은 androidx.test:runner, androidx.test:monitor, androidx.test.uiautomator:uiautomator를 추가한다. 구현 시점의 최신 안정 버전을 정확한 버전으로 고정한다.
  • UiAutomation 연결 플래그는 한 곳의 상수 UA_FLAGS = UiAutomation.FLAG_DONT_SUPPRESS_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES로 두고, Configurator.getInstance().uiAutomationFlags에도 같은 값을 넣는다.
  • androidx.test로 바꾼 경로가 아래 기준선을 해치거나 결과를 바꾸면 그 경로는 지금 코드를 유지하고, 이유를 코드 주석에 한 줄 남긴다(spec 5.1).
  • Task 1의 확인 1(소켓 도달)이나 확인 2(monkey 켜기·끄기)가 실패하면 프로젝트를 중단한다. 대체 방식(TCP + adb forward, setActivityController)으로 가지 않는다.
  • 성능 기준선(SDK 36 에뮬레이터 Medium_Phone)에서 잡음을 넘는 회귀가 없어야 한다.
  • 유휴 ui 약 265ms
  • tap→하위 화면 중앙값 약 976ms
  • Recents 키 응답 약 627ms
  • 드래그 약 126ms
  • 첫 dump_active 약 158ms
  • 기기 작업은 저장소 규칙을 따른다.
  • 에뮬레이터는 android emulator start Medium_Phone으로 띄운다. 새 AVD는 만들지 않는다.
  • 프로세스는 이 저장소 target\ 바이너리만 PID로 종료한다. 이미지 이름으로 taskkill하지 않는다.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. am instrument 프로세스가 죽은 경우 (USB 재연결, adb kill-server 등): 데몬도 죽는다. 다음 명령은 "no daemon … start it with mobax use"로 실패해야 하고, use는 재설치 없이 다시 띄워야 한다. → Task 7 Step 7
  2. 기기에 다른 서명으로 설치돼 있는 경우 (다른 PC나 CI에서 만든 빌드): use가 자동으로 지우고 다시 설치해야 한다. → Task 7 Step 1(파싱 테스트), Step 7(기기 확인)
  3. 읽을 수 없는 파일을 cp로 받거나 쓸 수 없는 경로로 보내는 경우: 오류로 끝나야 한다. "pulled 0 bytes" 같은 성공으로 끝나면 안 된다. → Task 4 Step 4
  4. 데몬이 비정상 종료한 경우 (크래시, am force-stop): 기기가 monkey 상태로 남으면 안 된다. → Task 1 확인 2, Task 8 Step 3
  5. 다른 UiAutomation이 이미 연결돼 있는 경우 (사용자의 UiAutomator 테스트 실행 중): use가 6초 타임아웃으로 멈추지 말고 원인을 담은 오류를 내야 한다. → Task 2 Step 5

docs.title: Task 1: 위험 확인 스파이크 (버리는 코드)
docs.text:
이 작업의 코드는 커밋하지 않는다. 결과만 계획 문서 끝의 "스파이크 결과" 절에 적고 커밋한다.

Files: - Create (임시, 커밋 안 함): src/dev/mobileax/daemon/SpikeInstrumentation.kt - Modify (임시, 커밋 안 함): AndroidManifest.xml, build.gradle.kts(minSdk = 31, release signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug")) - Modify (커밋): 이 계획 문서 끝에 "스파이크 결과" 절 추가

Interfaces: - Produces: 확인 1~5의 성공·실패 기록. 실패한 항목이 있으면 이후 Task의 범위가 바뀐다.

  • [ ] Step 1: 스파이크 instrumentation 작성

SpikeInstrumentation : androidx.test.runner.MonitoringInstrumentation이 하는 일. 스파이크 동안에만 build.gradle.kts에 Task 2의 androidx.test 의존성을 임시로 추가한다. - onCreate(main 스레드)에서 LocalServerSocket("mobaxd_spike")를 연다. - 별도 스레드에서 accept하고, 길이 접두(uint32 BE) 프레임 ping에 pong으로 답한다. 와이어 형식과 같다. - start()는 부르지 않는다. - 아래 결과를 sendStatus(0, Bundle().apply { putString("spike", line) })로 내보낸다. - ActivityManager.getService().setUserIsMonkey(true)(리플렉션) 결과 - ActivityManager.isUserAMonkey() 값 - Work 스레드에서 getUiAutomation()으로 연결한 결과 - 3-arg injectInputEvent(ev, false, false) 리플렉션 결과 - adoptShellPermissionIdentity() 아래에서 확인 4의 각 항목 결과 - 확인 6: Configurator.getInstance().uiAutomationFlags = UA_FLAGS 후 UiDevice.getInstance(this)를 만들고, 그 uiAutomation이 getUiAutomation(UA_FLAGS)와 같은 인스턴스(===)인지 - 확인 7: super.onCreate(arguments)만 부르고 start()는 부르지 않은 상태에서, 5분 동안 프로세스와 am instrument -w가 살아 있는지. MonitoringInstrumentation이 스스로 finish()하지 않는지를 본다.

manifest에는 다음을 추가한다. 

<instrumentation android:name="dev.mobileax.daemon.SpikeInstrumentation" android:targetPackage="dev.mobileax.daemon" />

  • [ ] Step 2: 빌드·설치·실행
./gradlew -q mobaxJar
adb push build/mobax.jar /data/local/tmp/mobaxd.apk
adb shell pm install -r -t /data/local/tmp/mobaxd.apk
adb shell "nohup am instrument -w --no-hidden-api-checks dev.mobileax.daemon/.SpikeInstrumentation > /data/local/tmp/spike.log 2>&1 &"

Expected: pm install → Success. spike.log에 INSTRUMENTATION_STATUS: spike=… 줄들이 찍힌다.

  • [ ] Step 3: 확인 1, 소켓 도달 (실패하면 중단)

adb forward tcp:19999 localabstract:mobaxd_spike
ping 프레임을 보내 pong을 받는다. 이어서 CLI의 adb server 경로(host:transport:SERIAL + localabstract:mobaxd_spike)로도 확인한다. mobax-core::adb_server::device_stream을 쓰는 임시 Rust 테스트나 mobax dev ping --port로 하고, 커밋하지 않는다.

확인이 끝나면 adb forward --remove tcp:19999로 정리한다.

Expected: 두 경로 모두 pong.

  • [ ] Step 4: 확인 2, monkey 켜기·끄기 (실패하면 중단)

  • spike.log에서 setUserIsMonkey 성공과 isUserAMonkey=true를 확인한다.

  • adb shell am force-stop dev.mobileax.daemon 후 monkey 설정 없이 스파이크를 다시 띄워서 isUserAMonkey=false가 보고되는지 확인한다. 끝난 instrumentation이 표시를 되돌리는지 보는 것이다.
  • 크래시 경로도 확인한다. 스파이크가 일부러 throw하게 한 번 실행한 뒤 다시 띄워 false인지 본다.

Expected: 켜짐 → true. force-stop 후와 크래시 후 → false.

AMS main 소스상으로는 instrumentation이 끝나 UiAutomation 연결이 정리될 때(SHUTDOWN_UI_AUTOMATION_CONNECTION_MSG) mUserIsMonkey = false로 되돌린다. 이 확인은 그 동작이 에뮬레이터에서도 같은지 보는 것이다. false로 돌아오지 않으면 실패로 보지 말고, drop이 setUserIsMonkey(false)를 직접 불러야 한다는 결론으로 기록한다.

  • [ ] Step 5: 확인 3~5 (실패해도 중단하지 않고 사용자에게 보고)

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: build.gradle.kts - minSdk = 31 - implementation에 androidx.test:runner, androidx.test:monitor, androidx.test.uiautomator:uiautomator를 추가한다(정확한 버전 고정) - release signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug") - 머리 주석과 mobaxJar 설명을 instrumentation 기준으로 바꾼다. - Modify: AndroidManifest.xml. <instrumentation android:name="dev.mobileax.daemon.MobaxInstrumentation" android:targetPackage="dev.mobileax.daemon" />를 넣는다. 주석은 "installed and run via am instrument"로 바꾼다. - Create: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/MobaxInstrumentation.kt - Modify: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Main.kt. 진입점 역할을 없애고 init 로직(initDaemon, enableInteractiveWindows)만 internal object DaemonInit으로 남긴다. 파일 이름은 DaemonInit.kt로 바꿔도 된다. - Modify: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Binders.kt. systemContextLazy, appContextLazy, shellApplication()을 지우고 service(), asInterface(), iPackageManager() 등 binder 도우미만 남긴다. - Modify: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Logx.kt. boot/bootWarn이 System.err와 함께 Instrumentation.sendStatus로도 내보낸다. - Modify: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Screenshot.kt. initDisplayManager()가 Binders.appContext() 대신 ctx를 쓰고, shell 이름 wrapper를 지운다. - Modify: proguard-rules.pro. MobaxInstrumentation을 keep한다. manifest에서 이름으로 참조되기 때문이다. androidx.test가 리플렉션으로 찾는 클래스 때문에 R8 경고나 런타임 오류가 나면 해당 keep 규칙만 추가한다. - Create: src/dev/mobileax/daemon/Daemon.kt

Interfaces: - Produces: - class MobaxInstrumentation : androidx.test.runner.MonitoringInstrumentation - Daemon.kt의 최상위 선언. 상태를 갖지 않고 InstrumentationRegistry에서 읽기만 한다. 이후 Task의 Shell과 각 핸들러가 쓴다. - internal const val UA_FLAGS: Int = UiAutomation.FLAG_DONT_SUPPRESS_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES - internal val instr: Instrumentation get() = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation() - internal val ctx: Context get() = instr.context - internal val ua: UiAutomation get() = instr.getUiAutomation(UA_FLAGS) (같은 플래그면 캐시된 인스턴스가 나온다) - internal val device: UiDevice by lazy { Configurator.getInstance().uiAutomationFlags = UA_FLAGS; UiDevice.getInstance(instr) } - Logx.status(line: String) - 인자 -e port N(기본 9008) - Consumes: Loop.init(), MobaxServer, Dispatch, Server.Handlers(sysCtx 이름은 ctx로 바꾼다)

  • [ ] Step 1: MobaxInstrumentation 작성

  • onCreate(arguments: Bundle) (main 스레드, ActivityThread의 main looper가 이미 돈다):

  • super.onCreate(arguments). InstrumentationRegistry가 이때 등록된다.
  • port = InstrumentationRegistry.getArguments().getString("port")?.toInt() ?: 9008
  • Loop.init()
  • MobaxServer(port, Dispatch(ready, onQuit = { … }))를 시작한다. onQuit은 서버를 닫고 finish(0, Bundle())을 부른다.
  • Loop.scope.launch { ready.complete(DaemonInit.init()) }
  • start()는 부르지 않는다. onStart를 쓰지 않기 때문이다. Task 1 확인 7이 다른 방식을 정했으면 그 방식을 따른다.
  • DaemonInit.init() (withContext(Loop.Work)):
  • ua를 처음 읽어 연결한다(getUiAutomation(UA_FLAGS)). 현재 connect(1)과 같은 플래그다. 이어서 device를 만들어 같은 인스턴스를 쓰게 한다.
  • ua.adoptShellPermissionIdentity()
  • ua.setRunAsMonkey(true). 실패하면 Logx.bootWarn만 남긴다.
  • enableInteractiveWindows(ua)
  • 지금처럼 핸들러를 조립하고 warmup을 띄운다.
  • 지울 것:
  • disableHiddenApiRestrictions: --no-hidden-api-checks가 대신한다.
  • initLikeActivityThreadMain, setDdmAppName, logSlowMainLooper(main looper는 이제 ActivityThread 소유), connectedUiAutomation, createUiAutomation, connectWithRetry, invokeConnect, registerShutdownHook
  • 부팅 줄은 지금과 같은 문구로 남긴다: mobaxd listening on @mobaxd_N, mobaxd ready (sdk=N).

  • monkey 줄을 추가한다: mobaxd monkey before=<false|true> after=<false|true>. before는 setRunAsMonkey 전에 읽은 ActivityManager.isUserAMonkey()이고, after는 그 후의 값이다. dumpsys에는 이 상태가 나오지 않아서, Task 8의 해제 확인이 이 before 값을 쓴다.

  • [ ] Step 2: Logx.status 구현

InstrumentationRegistry가 등록된 뒤라면(등록 전에는 getInstrumentation()이 예외를 던지므로 잡아서 구분한다) instr.sendStatus(0, Bundle().apply { putString("mobaxd", line) })를 부르고, 아니면 System.err만 쓴다. boot/bootWarn/fatal이 이를 부른다.

Run: ./gradlew -q mobaxJar Expected: 종료 코드 0, build/mobax.jar 생성.

그 뒤 MOBILEAX_JAR가 아닌 기존 CLI로 mobax ui, mobax tap X Y, mobax see out.png를 실행한다. 지금 CLI의 빠른 경로는 ping만 보므로 그대로 붙는다.

Expected: - mobax.log에 mobaxd listening, mobaxd ready, mobaxd monkey before=false after=true가 있다. - 세 명령이 정상이다. - see의 미러 로그에 wrapper 언급이 없다(adb logcat -d | grep "screenshot: display ctx").

  • [ ] Step 5: UiAutomation 연결 실패를 원인과 함께 보고하기 (Review Focus 5)

getUiAutomation이 예외를 던지면(이미 다른 UiAutomation이 연결된 경우) 다음을 한다. - Logx.fatal("UiAutomation unavailable: <예외 메시지> — another UiAutomation (e.g. a UiAutomator test) may be connected", t) - finish(2, Bundle().apply { putString("mobaxd", "fatal: …") })

확인 방법: Step 4의 데몬이 떠 있는 상태에서 같은 명령으로 두 번째 instrumentation을 띄운다(-e port 9010). 같은 패키지라 AMS가 첫 번째를 정리할 수 있으니, 결과를 그대로 기록한다. 그다음 uiautomator dump를 데몬이 떠 있는 동안 실행해 데몬 로그와 uiautomator 출력을 확인한다.

Expected: mobax.log에 fatal: UiAutomation unavailable 줄이 있고, 데몬이 멈춘 채 남아 있지 않다.
